narrative_purpose: Contrasts the two ways a flier leaves the ground - the bird's hind-leg leap (which carries dead launch-weight aloft) versus the pterosaur's forelimb vault (launch limbs and flight limbs are one) - the mechanic the chapter says Pandora's giants inherit.
subject: Two three-stage launch sequences side by side against a dark page. LEFT, a large bird: stage one crouched on its hind legs, stage two leaping straight up off those legs, stage three airborne with wings spreading while the heavy hind legs hang beneath it as dead weight. RIGHT, a giant pterosaur: stage one crouched on all four limbs, stage two vaulting forward and up off its powerful folded forelimbs like a pole-vaulter, stage three airborne unfurling those same forelimbs into wings. The two sequences are clearly separated, each reading left-to-right as motion.
